item.research_question: Can a high-entropy nitride based spectrally selective film (SSF) be used to enhance the warming performance of a textile?
item.material_system: High-entropy nitride (ZrNbMo-Al-N) based SSF on cotton
item.test_conditions: Solar radiation intensity of 0.6 suns, at 0 °C, and ambient temperature of 7.5 °C
key_findings: The SSF-decorated cotton achieves a high solar absorptance of 92.8% and a low IR emittance of 39.2%.
The textile realizes a 3.5 °C drop in the indoor set-point, which is of substantial significance for indoor building heating energy savings.
The cotton/Al/SSF textile could heat the human body even at low solar irradiance intensity in severely cold weather.
The textile retains good breathability and durability of the original cloth.
The solar absorptance of the SSF-decorated textile is 9.1% higher than that of the best-performing radiative warming textiles.
item.mechanism: The collective effects of destructive interference and intrinsic absorption of high-entropy nitride ZrNbMo-Al-N boost sunlight harvesting ability.
item.future_work: To broaden the working scenarios, such as outdoors on cloudy days or at night, by depositing the well-designed SSF on an Al-decorated Nano-PE.
quotes: High-entropy nitride is a category of up-and-coming photothermal materials due to its unique and fascinating structural characteristics, and large compositional space.
The resultant textile embraces a superior spectral selectivity (α/ε = 92.8%/39.2%), which simultaneously enables solar heating and passive radiative warming.
The cotton/Al/SSF textile realizes a 3.5 °C drop in the indoor set-point, which is of substantial significance for indoor building heating energy savings.
